claims.text: HfZrTiTa0.53 has a reported yield strength of 786 MPa.
HfZrTiTa0.53 has a reported compressive strength of 1314 MPa.
HfZrTiTa0.53 has a reported terminal tensile strain of 13.5%.
The reported HfZrTiTa0.53 properties were measured at room temperature under quasi-static loading.
The proposed intervention is 8–15% cold rolling followed by controlled sub-transus annealing.
The proposed cold-rolling and annealing treatment will produce a fully recrystallized ultrafine-grained microstructure in HfZrTiTa0.53.
The ultrafine-grained structure will have increased grain-boundary density.
The treated microstructure will enhance dislocation slip during tensile loading.
The treated HfZrTiTa0.53 may activate mechanical nanotwinning during tensile loading.
Grain refinement provides additional obstacles to dislocation motion and thereby elevates strain-hardening capacity.
Mechanical nanotwinning can delay necking to higher tensile strains.
The treatment will increase uniform elongation from approximately 13.5% to 25–30%.
The treated alloy will retain a yield strength near 780 MPa.
The treated alloy will retain a compressive strength near 1314 MPa.
The treatment will preserve impact-triggered chemical energy release.
The ductility prediction applies at room temperature under quasi-static tensile loading at approximately 1×10^-3 s^-1.
The treatment should not adversely affect high-temperature or high-strain-rate performance.

contradictions.description: The 13.5% baseline is identified as terminal tensile strain or strain at fracture, but it is then used as the baseline for uniform elongation. Fracture elongation and uniform elongation are distinct quantities, so the predicted increase and falsification threshold do not use a consistently defined endpoint.

The conditions and predicted outcome require assessment of dynamic impact energy release and preservation of high-strain-rate or high-temperature behavior, whereas the boundary says effectiveness is validated only at room temperature under quasi-static loading. The falsification rule also lacks a threshold for impact-energy preservation.
